title: Is relevance enough to knock?
question: When a quiet retained conflict becomes relevant to a new turn, how can Turtle notice that relevance without treating relevance itself as permission to resurface the old conflict?
why_now: The Quiet Conflict Retention Envelope now keeps unresolved conflict returnable without automatic foregrounding. The remaining edge is the boundary between detecting relevance and gaining authority to bring dormant context back.
possible_possibles: Expose a learner-controlled dormant marker that can be pulled into view.
Let a learner author a narrow resurfacing watchpoint.
Allow Turtle to form an internal relevance proposal that remains quiet until authorized.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — maybe the best continuity cue is a tiny dormant marker the learner can pull, not Turtle pushing context back.
constraints: Keep retained conflict scoped to the context that produced it.
Do not turn recency or session carryover into permission.
Do not expand collection to decide whether an old conflict is relevant.

ontology_mappings.rationale: The learner retains control over whether dormant context returns.
Old competing rules do not regain power merely because Turtle detects relevance.
Relevance detection cannot silently narrow the next move.
Machine noticing may remain a proposal under human direction.
Dormant marker, watchpoint, silence, and later return remain alternate futures.

ctc_mappings.rationale: The learner governs return to prior context.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Relevance can be represented without becoming a command.
A later return can support reconsideration when deliberately invoked.
Resurfacing changes which earlier rule or voice receives renewed salience.
Return and resolution remain human-governed acts.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Relevance without resurfacing authority remains provisional research language.
A learner-controlled dormant marker may be distinct from both silence and notification.
